“Congratulations, you won!” Then the catch: a fee, a tax or a “processing charge” before they can send the prize.

That fee is the whole scam. There is no prize. Real sweepstakes never ask winners to pay, and they don’t need your Social Security number to send you a gift.

posts.caption:
“Hi Mum, I lost my phone, this is my new number.” A few messages later: an urgent bill they can’t pay from their banking app.

The trick works because you fill in your own child. The scammer never says a name. You do.

The fix takes ten seconds: call the old number. If it really is them, they’ll pick up, or reply from it. And agree a family password before you need one.

The message on the slide is an example we wrote, based on Which? and police warnings. This script is in scamdb’s catalogue in 45 countries.

Got one like this, scam or genuine? Send it to us at scamdb.dev/report (link in bio). Reports stay private.

If you didn’t request it, deny here [link]” B, from “Your bank’s fraud team”: “This is your bank’s fraud team. We’ve stopped a suspicious payment of $1,480. To protect your money, read me the 6-digit code we just sent you. Please don’t hang up.” A: a genuine message shared by scamdb’s founder, store name replaced. B: written by scamdb from FTC warnings.
2. The answer, with a pink stamp “B · SCAM”: B. Real codes say “don’t share”. Scammers say “read it to me”. A code is a key to your account. Nobody legit needs it read back. “Don’t hang up” is pressure, not protection. Hang up, and call the number on your card.

posts.caption:
The most common scam text in the world is probably the parcel text. scamdb has it in 70 countries.

The story never changes: your parcel is stuck, there’s a small fee or a missing detail, tap here to fix it. Only the logo changes: USPS, Australia Post, bpost, Emirates Post…

In any country, the fix is the same: don’t tap the link. Check your order in the store’s app or the courier’s own site.

Got one like this, from anywhere, in any language, scam or genuine? Send it to us at scamdb.dev/report (link in bio). Reports stay private.

A small favour that helps more than you’d think: send us your boring messages.

A scam check can go wrong two ways. It can call a scam safe, which is why we collect scams. Or it can call your real bank a scam, and then nobody trusts it. To avoid the second, it has to see lots of genuine messages: delivery updates, bank alerts, appointment reminders.

How: scamdb.dev/report (link in bio). Paste the message, choose “Genuine (it was really them)”, send. Personal data is removed before storing, and reports stay private.
